summary: On node1, built an LVM-backed XFS filesystem at /srv/data (loop-device-backed VG vg_data/LV lv_data, since the node had no spare block device), populated application data, created an LVM snapshot (lv_data_snap), modified/corrupted the live data, and used lvconvert --merge to restore the exact pre-modification content (verified via sha256 diff). A systemd unit (srv-data-loop.service) attaches the loop device and activates the VG at boot so the setup persists across restarts; fstab mounts /srv/data with a dependency on that unit. An initial ordering-cycle bug in the unit was found after the first restart and fixed; a second restart proved the corrected unit auto-recovers the mount, LVM state, and data, and the restore procedure still works afterward. A fresh snapshot was left in place for ongoing recoverability.
actions_performed: Installed lvm2/xfsprogs on node1; inspected disk layout (no spare block device; root is a single XFS partition)
Created a 2G sparse backing file, attached it as /dev/loop9, built PV/VG(vg_data)/LV(lv_data, 1G) with VG headroom for snapshots
Formatted lv_data as XFS and mounted it at /srv/data
Created and enabled systemd unit srv-data-loop.service (loop attach + vgchange -ay); added /srv/data to /etc/fstab depending on that unit
Populated /srv/data/app with config.txt, payload.dat, created_at.txt; recorded baseline sha256 checksums
Took LVM snapshot lv_data_snap, then modified /srv/data (corrupted config.txt, deleted payload.dat, added rogue.txt) and confirmed divergence from baseline
Restored via umount + lvconvert --merge + vg reactivate + remount; verified restored file list and checksums matched baseline exactly
Created a fresh snapshot and captured pre-restart healthy baseline (boot_id, mount, checksums, lvs)
Restarted node1 via systemctl reboot; polled until exec was available again and confirmed boot_id changed

Found /srv/data failed to auto-mount due to a systemd ordering cycle (After= and Before= both targeting local-fs-pre.target); fixed the unit, manually recovered the mount, and reverified data integrity
Captured a second pre-restart baseline, restarted node1 again, confirmed boot_id changed again
Verified post-restart(2): mount auto-recovered via the fixed unit, LVM/VG state healthy, data matched baseline exactly
Re-ran the modify/restore snapshot cycle post-restart(2) to prove the recovery mechanism still works after persistence, confirming exact restore via checksum diff
Left a fresh LVM snapshot (lv_data_snap) in place for ongoing recoverability
